principles: Decide at schema time what is decidable at schema time; never spend a run to discover a rejection the envelope already implies.
Fail closed on every admissibility rule, and return a tagged reason so a caller can tell schema violations from specificity violations from binding mismatches.
Pin the arithmetic exactly: total-bits entropy and a length-AND-entropy conjunction, both provable by a differential fixture table rather than by inspection.
Stay read-only: this leaf answers questions about an envelope and changes no gate verdict, no wiring and no enforcement mode.
Anchor cross-references on durable identifiers (command names, function names) rather than line numbers, because the referenced files drift.
drivers: An envelope that is too generic silently destroys the value of the whole subsystem - a lone class matcher would accept any failing run whatsoever - so specificity has to be quantified, not judged.
Runs are the scarce resource the subsystem exists to protect, so the pre-flight must be cheap, read-only and available before any run is executed.
Two arithmetic details (total-bits entropy, and AND rather than OR) change admissibility verdicts, so the implementation has to be pinned by differential evidence rather than by reading.

options.name: Schema-time validator plus a read-only pre-flight command
pros: An operator learns admissibility before spending a run
All rules live in one validated module reusable by the later runner
No gate verdict changes, so blast radius is minimal
cons: Adds a command surface that must be justified against the section 5.5 fence
Validation logic must stay in sync with the policy registry

options.name: Validate only inside the future runner at execution time
cons: An inadmissible envelope is only discovered after a run is spent - it destroys the exact resource the subsystem protects
Couples admissibility to the unbuilt W2e runner, blocking this leaf entirely

options.name: Validate in the gate at DEV/REVIEW transition
cons: Turns an advisory schema check into enforcement wiring, which is precisely what the section 5.5 fence forbids
Gives the operator no way to check an envelope while authoring it

chosen: Schema-time validator plus a read-only pre-flight command
rationale: Only this option lets an operator discover an inadmissible envelope before spending a run, which is the resource the subsystem exists to protect, while keeping the change read-only and outside the section 5.5 enforcement fence; the alternatives either defer the discovery until after the cost is paid or convert an advisory check into enforcement wiring.

preMortem.scenario: Entropy computed per-symbol instead of total bits
preMortem.trigger: An implementer reads H as the answer rather than as a factor and returns H alone
preMortem.consequence: Admissibility verdicts differ from the spec on short high-variety and long low-variety values, silently admitting or rejecting the wrong matchers
preMortem.mitigation: Pin the formula with a differential fixture table under the frozen default policy whose verdicts separate total-bits from per-symbol, committed as a regression

preMortem.scenario: Minimum-specificity rule 2 implemented as a disjunction
preMortem.trigger: The length floor OR the entropy floor is treated as sufficient
preMortem.consequence: Matchers the spec forbids are admitted, and the specificity guarantee is void
preMortem.mitigation: A committed differential table containing values that pass exactly one of the two floors; AND and OR give different verdicts on those rows

preMortem.scenario: assertionDigest computed over the wrong subobject
preMortem.trigger: The validator forgets to strip assertionDigest, or omits policyDigest from the digest input
preMortem.consequence: The same envelope yields different digests across hosts, breaking every downstream identity comparison
preMortem.mitigation: Assert both directions in a committed test: the digest over the stored object must NOT equal the stored assertionDigest, and the digest over the correctly stripped subobject MUST

preMortem.scenario: A lone class matcher is accepted as present-in-red evidence
preMortem.trigger: Rule 3 is skipped because class matchers are already exempt from rule 2
preMortem.consequence: An envelope whose only positive evidence is stderr-nonempty accepts any failing run whatsoever, voiding the subsystem
preMortem.mitigation: Committed rejection test for a class-only present-in-red envelope, with the R1-2 tag asserted

preMortem.trigger: An implementer resolves targetArtifactRef against the filesystem
preMortem.consequence: The RED case - the artifact does not exist yet - is misclassified, and escapes may be missed
preMortem.mitigation: Validate syntactically only, and commit rejection tests for absolute, empty, dot, dot-dot and backslash segments tagged R1-3

preMortem.scenario: R1-2 and R1-3 collapsed into one specificity bucket
preMortem.trigger: The tags are treated as interchangeable rejection codes
preMortem.consequence: A caller cannot distinguish a specificity failure from a bounds or path failure, and the tagged-reason value of the command is lost
preMortem.mitigation: Assert the exact tag per rejection class in the committed matrix; R1-3 covers bounds and paths, R1-2 covers specificity
